*Experts offer insights on fueling, enjoying meals, hydration, movement and a 20-day Holiday Hustle workout plan*


**Key Highlights:**


- Life Time experts share six tips: Fuel up before the festivities, anchor meals with protein and fiber, stay hydrated, keep moving, enjoy meals in moderation and make time for stress relief.
- Advice comes from Life Time's nutrition, coaching, performance and studio leaders.
- Small, consistent habits matter more than perfection.
- Life Time's complimentary 20-day Holiday Hustle program, available to members in the Life Time app and starting Nov. 30, helps keep them moving and consistent through the holidays.
- Life Time brings fitness, pickleball, recovery, spa services, healthy dining, its Kids Academy and work spaces under one roof.


CHANHASSEN, Minn.


, Nov. 25, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / --[Life Time](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4831207-1&h=286718642&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.lifetime.life%2F&a=Life+Time) (NYSE: LTH), the nation's premier healthy lifestyle brand, is sharing six practical, expert-backed tips to help people enjoy the season without losing their routine as Thanksgiving approaches and the busiest stretch of the holiday calendar kicks off. Life Time is also inviting members to join the Holiday Hustle, a complimentary, trainer-led 20-day program in the Life Time app that begins Nov. 30.


The advice comes from Chella Wahlin, Registered Dietitian at Life Time; David Freeman, Senior Director of Signature Coach Excellence at Life Time; Danny King, Director of Performance and Recovery at Life Time; and Meggan Berg, Studio Leader at Life Time Baybrook in Texas.


Their guidance shares common threads: Consistency matters more than perfection. Enjoy the holidays, including the foods you love most. And small, repeatable habits around eating, hydration, movement and stress make it easier to enjoy holiday traditions and get back to a full routine after.


**Six expert tips for a healthier holiday season:**


**1. Arrive fueled, not famished** Skipping meals to save room for big holiday meals tends to backfire. "One of the biggest mistakes I hear is showing up to a holiday party without having eaten much, or anything at all, leading up to it that day," said Chella Wahlin, Registered Dietitian at Life Time. She recommends high-protein foods paired with colorful vegetables earlier in the day to build a base of fiber, protein and antioxidants, so you can choose what you want to try rather than eating from a place of hunger.


David Freeman, Senior Director of Signature Coach Excellence at Life Time, agrees: "Eat regular meals leading up to it, stay hydrated, and give yourself permission to enjoy your favorites. You don't need to earn your food or punish yourself afterward."


**2. Anchor your plate with protein and fiber** "I like to recommend grounding the meal or snack with 30 grams of protein to support fullness, craving regulation, and energy levels," Wahlin said.


Danny King, Director of Performance and Recovery at Life Time, applies the same idea to the meals surrounding the main event: "All the meals around the main holiday meals, focus on getting protein and fiber. It will keep you full, balance blood sugar and minimize any negative impact."


If an appetizer-and-dessert party leaves little protein on the table, Wahlin leans on a serving of[LTH Vital Vegan Protein](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4831207-1&h=3722172072&u=https%3A%2F%2Fshop.lifetime.life%2Flth-vital-vegan-protein&a=LTH+Vital+Vegan+Protein) beforehand.


**3. Hydrate before and between treats** Hydration has an outsized effect on hunger and cravings, Wahlin notes, and it can help you feel better the next day. She suggests drinking plenty of water leading up to a party and building in intentional hydration between holiday drinks and treats. Another one of her go-to supplements is[LTH Hydrate electrolytes](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4831207-1&h=1713976834&u=https%3A%2F%2Fshop.lifetime.life%2Flth-hydrate&a=LTH+Hydrate+electrolytes) , a sugar-free electrolyte booster that can be sprinkled into a glass of water or turned into a festive mocktail.


**4. Make movement a daily appointment** "A workout, a daily walk, or 15 minutes between commitments all count," Freeman said. "Keep showing up in ways that fit your schedule - consistency matters more than perfection."


King also recommends shorter workouts and walks after meals: "It will make getting back into a full routine easier, minimize the damage of holiday meals and really help you feel better."


**5. Enjoy the holiday meal and give yourself grace** Berg, Studio Leader at Life Time Baybrook in Texas, says everything can fit into a healthy lifestyle in moderation: "If you overindulge at a meal or enjoy an extra dessert, don't beat yourself up. You're human." Exercise, she adds, is "a celebration of what your body can do, not a punishment for what you ate," and "one meal never defines your overall health."


**6. Build in stress relief and fill your cup** The holidays can be a stressful time, and stress can make every habit above harder to keep. King's advice: "Acknowledge that and add some stress relieving activities to your weekly routine."


Berg encourages people to stay committed to "filling your cup," which doesn't have to mean a normal workout: "Taking a walk, getting to a fitness class, spending a few moments in silence, practicing gratitude, or simply making time for yourself."


For members who want a little extra structure, Life Time's Holiday Hustle is a complimentary 20-day program led by Life Time trainers, starting Nov. 30 in the[Life Time app](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4831207-1&h=3401895219&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.lifetime.life%2Fdigital-app.html&a=Life+Time+app) . Members can choose from a library of strength workouts based on their goals, schedule and equipment, at the club or at home, or opt for bodyweight workouts, on-demand classes, mobility sessions or walks. Each day centers on three simple habits: Move your body, eat about 30 grams of protein per meal and drink at least half your body weight in ounces of water. Members can also book a complimentary 50-minute Intro to Dynamic Personal Training Session to get expert support. Enrollment is open now.


Holiday calendars leave little wiggle room. Rather than splitting a week among a gym, a boutique studio, a pickleball facility, a spa and a coworking space, Life Time members can find strength training, group fitness, pickleball, recovery, spa services, healthy food, child care through its Kids Academy and workspace under one roof, all with one membership. That means a morning class, a protein-forward, healthy lunch, a recovery session and a work call can happen in one stop, a practical advantage when the to-do list grows and consistency is the goal.
